ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A right hexagonal prism has a height of 3 feet and each edge of the hexagonal bases is 6 inches. What is the sum of the areas of the non-hexagonal faces of the prism, in square feet? <image1>
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows an upright hexagonal prism: the upper and lower bases are congruent hexagons, and the non-hexagonal faces around the sides are vertical lateral faces. The problem text gives the prism height as 3 feet, and each side length of the hexagonal base as 6 inches. First unify the units: 6 inches = 0.5 feet. The sum of the areas of the non-base faces of a right prism is the lateral area, equal to the perimeter of the base multiplied by the height. The hexagon has 6 equal sides, so the base perimeter = 6 × 0.5 = 3 feet. Lateral area = 3 × 3 = 9 square feet.

method.method_draft: First observe the image: it depicts a right prism with congruent hexagonal top and bottom bases, and the non-hexagonal faces are the vertical side faces around the prism. Read from the text that the prism height is 3 feet and each edge of the hexagonal base is 6 inches. Convert 6 inches to 0.5 feet. Use the lateral surface area rule for a right prism: sum of non-base face areas = perimeter of base × height. The hexagonal base has 6 equal edges, so its perimeter is 6 × 0.5 = 3 feet. Then compute 3 × 3 = 9 square feet.
